method: Independent third-party adjudication against exact pinned source/catalog/context and authoritative language dictionaries or current CLDR data where applicable.

sources.title: MyAnonAMouse language filter enum and provider option pipeline
sources.supports: Selected sources are language names in MyAnonaMouseSearchLanguages and are rendered as standalone provider select-option labels; neighboring option labels provide catalog style context.

sources.title: Pinned language option catalogs and source registry
sources.supports: Provides the exact source key, current target values, neighboring target labels, locale files, and protected-literal rules at the pinned PR tree.

sources.title: Duden: Chinesisch
sources.supports: Chinesisch is the neuter noun meaning the Chinese language.

sources.title: Duden: Koreanisch
sources.supports: Koreanisch is the neuter noun meaning the Korean language.

sources.title: Duden: Pandschabi
sources.supports: Pandschabi is the neuter noun for the language.

sources.title: Duden: Kroatisch
sources.supports: Kroatisch is the neuter noun meaning the Croatian language.

sources.title: Duden: Kroatische
sources.supports: Kroatische is a substantivized adjective with the use restriction “only with a definite article”; this option has no article.

sources.title: Duden: Malaiisch
sources.supports: Malaiisch is the neuter noun for the language spoken on the Malay Peninsula and western Indonesia.

sources.title: Duden: malaysisch
sources.supports: malaysisch is an adjective relating to Malaysia or Malaysians, not the language name in this context.

sources.title: Arabic Academy of Cairo research PDF on Iceland
sources.supports: Uses الأيسلندية for the Icelandic language.

sources.title: RAE-ASALE DLE: guyaratí
sources.supports: Defines guyaratí as the Indian language spoken mainly in Guyarat.

sources.title: RAE-ASALE DLE: manés, manesa
sources.supports: Defines manés as the Celtic language spoken on the Isle of Man.

sources.title: FundéuRAE: panyabí / punyabí
sources.supports: Recommends punyabí for the language/gentilic.

sources.title: Larousse English–French: Greek
sources.supports: Translates ancient Greek as grec ancien.

sources.title: Larousse French–English: pendjabi
sources.supports: Translates French pendjabi as Punjabi.

sources.title: Dicionário Priberam: panjabi
sources.supports: Defines panjabi as an Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Panjab region.

sources.title: Kotobank / Britannica: Scottish Gaelic
sources.supports: Uses スコットランド・ゲーリック語 as the Japanese name for Scottish Gaelic.

sources.title: Unicode CLDR 49 release notes

sources.title: Locale-name lexical cross-check
sources.url: See the source-specific dictionary and CLDR entries in this file.
sources.supports: For sampled rows retained as current, the cross-review checked language-name recognition in the pinned standalone-option context; this ID is a method tag, not an independent lexicographic citation.

sources.title: Indonesian Farsi/Persia usage review note
sources.supports: The cross-review marked this choice for native-speaker adjudication; no source URL was recorded, and this note is not relied on to select a target.

sources.title: Unicode CLDR 22 Indonesian Persian display name
sources.supports: Historical Indonesian CLDR data used Persia for Persian; not used as current release evidence.
